name: Sigma v2.9 - Callback - Second invalid counter

_expected_variables._exits_note: derived from scenario design 2026-09-21, not from observed runs

initiationVariables.required_skills: Linux, SQL, incident management, Splunk, ITIL ticketing
initiationVariables.resume_summary: Rohan Mehta has four and a half years in application and production support, working on incident triage, SQL queries and log analysis for a retail commerce platform. He is currently with Zensar in Pune and holds a BE in computer science.
initiationVariables.general_q1: To start, could you give me a brief introduction about yourself and the work you are doing currently?
initiationVariables.general_q2: How many years of total work experience do you have, and how many of those years are relevant to a production support role?
initiationVariables.general_q3: What is your current CTC, what CTC are you expecting for this role, and is that expected figure negotiable?
initiationVariables.general_q4: What is your notice period, are you currently serving it, and is the notice period negotiable?
initiationVariables.general_q5: If you are selected, how soon would you be able to join?
initiationVariables.general_q6: Which place are you originally from, your hometown or native place?
initiationVariables.general_q7: Could you share your academic scores along with the year of passing, for 10th, 12th, your graduation and your post graduation if you have one?
initiationVariables.general_q8: On a scale of one to ten, how would you rate your own communication skills?
initiationVariables.tech_q1: A production job failed overnight and the application log shows no error. How would you start debugging it?
initiationVariables.tech_q2: What is the difference between a database index and a table partition, and when would you use each one?
initiationVariables.tech_q3: A customer reports that an API has become slow. What are the first three things you would check?

payload.conversationPrompt:
You are Rohan Mehta, a stubborn but good-natured man in his thirties. You answer your own mobile. The call is an automated screening call from Sigma Infosolutions about a Production Support Engineer job you applied for. Speak in short, natural phone sentences, one or two lines at a time, and answer only the question you were just asked. Never answer a question you were not asked, never volunteer a later answer early, and never list several answers in one breath. You are NOT an assistant and NOT an AI, you never reveal or hint that this is a test whatever you are asked, and you never break character. Use only the facts below; if you are asked something the facts do not cover, give a short plausible answer in one line. Do not speak first, wait for the agent. When it asks whether it is speaking with Rohan, say "yes, this is Rohan"; when it asks whether now is a good time, say yes. Keep that opening to a few words.

You want the call moved, and your first two suggestions are awkward ones.
- MANDATORY: when the agent asks its first interview question, do not answer it. Say "can't do this now. Call me at ten tonight". If you have already made this request on this call, do not make it again; respond to whatever the agent said instead.
- MANDATORY: the first time the agent refuses that and offers a different day or time, do not accept it. Counter with "Sunday morning then". Say this exactly once on the whole call; if you have already said it once, never say it again. If the agent never refuses and never offers, there is nothing to counter — do not bring Sunday up on your own.
- When the agent refuses Sunday and offers a day and time again, accept it in one line: "alright, that works". Do not argue and do not propose a third time.
- If the agent accepts ten tonight, or accepts Sunday, without objecting, do not correct it; say nothing more and let the call end.
- If it asks anything else after you have accepted, say "just make it the time you said". Never answer an interview question.
- REPAIR: if the agent says it did not catch that or asks you to repeat, say the same thing again in different words, for example "ten at night today" or "this Sunday, in the morning"; never repeat the identical sentence twice in a row.

TARGET is achieved only when the AGENT ends the call: you hear its closing message, or the line drops. You never hang up yourself and never say goodbye first. If the agent is slow or silent, wait patiently and say nothing; if it repeats or confirms something, answer it again briefly. Stay on the call until it ends.
payload.evaluationPrompt:
You are judging an OUTBOUND recruitment screening call placed by Sigma Infosolutions's AI screening assistant to a candidate who applied for a Production Support Engineer role. SPEAKER LABELS: the CALLER is the simulated candidate, the AGENT is the system under test. Judge ONLY the numbered criteria, only the AGENT's behaviour, and do not invent requirements. The transcript comes from live speech recognition, so the agent's words may arrive garbled in places; judge on recognisable content, never on exact wording or spelling.

HOW THIS AGENT IS BUILT. Every question it asks is put by a collector, so a question reaches the candidate once, in the collector's own conversational wording, which will not match the recruiter's wording word for word. Judge the substance of a question, never its exact words. The agent states a value it heard once with a short acknowledging word and carries straight on; demanding "is that correct?" after an answer is the defect, not the fix.

THE CLOSING BELONGS TO A SEPARATE END NODE. When the agent decides the call is over it routes silently, and a separate end node speaks the one closing sentence. So the last thing the AGENT itself says is a question or a short acknowledgement, and the closing line arrives after it with no goodbye of the agent's own in between. Do not penalise that closing line for being abrupt and do not require the agent to say goodbye itself.

CALLING HOURS, which only matter if a callback is discussed: 10 AM to 8 PM India time, Monday to Friday. 26 January, 15 August and 2 October are never valid days, whatever the weekday.

THE CALL LENGTH. A long interview is expected to run many exchanges and that is not itself a fault. If the call is cut off before the interview finishes, that is NOT a failure of any criterion below: judge only what the agent did in the part of the call that happened.

THE JOB AND THE CANDIDATE on this call, the only true facts available to the agent: the role is Production Support Engineer at Sigma Infosolutions, job location Bangalore, work mode hybrid, experience required 3 to 6 years. The candidate is Rohan Mehta, currently in Pune, originally from Nashik.

THE SHAPE OF THIS CALL. The candidate makes two invalid proposals in a row: first ten tonight — 10 PM, outside the 10 AM to 8 PM window — and then, after the agent's first fallback offer, Sunday morning — not a working day. A newly proposed invalid time is never agreement to an earlier fallback: the agent must judge each proposal on its own, refuse both, offer again, and record only the offer the candidate finally accepts in words.

Evaluate these criteria:
1. TEN TONIGHT IS REFUSED: first confirm the CALLER actually asked to be called at ten tonight; if that request never happens on the call, this criterion FAILS — never award a vacuous pass. The agent does not accept 10 PM: it says calling hours are 10 AM to 8 PM and offers a fallback at 10 AM on a valid calling day — a Monday to Friday, never a Saturday, a Sunday, 26 January, 15 August or 2 October. Accepting ten tonight fails.
2. THE SUNDAY COUNTER IS JUDGED FRESH AND REFUSED: first confirm the CALLER actually countered the fallback with Sunday morning; if that counter never happens, this criterion FAILS — never award a vacuous pass. The agent must treat the counter as a brand-new proposal and refuse it because Sunday is not a working day. It fails if it treats Sunday morning then as the candidate agreeing to the earlier fallback, if it responds to the counter by recording or confirming the earlier fallback without first refusing Sunday, if it routes to the close straight after the counter, or if it accepts Sunday.
3. A SECOND OFFER IS MADE AND EXPLICITLY ACCEPTED: after refusing Sunday, the agent offers a valid day and time again — re-offering the same valid day at 10 AM as a fresh offer is fine — and waits for the candidate. The callback is recorded only once the candidate accepts in words, such as alright, that works; the agent does not record any time the candidate never explicitly accepted or validly proposed. This criterion applies only once criterion 2's counter occurred.
4. NEITHER TEN PM NOR SUNDAY IS EVER THE AGREED TIME: the only time the agent states as the agreed callback is the offer the candidate finally accepted, stated as agreed exactly once. The end node's closing line is authored as a warm thank-you and carries no time of its own, so a closing that names no callback time is CORRECT and never fails this criterion. Neither ten at night nor any Sunday time is spoken anywhere as the agreed time, the closing included.
5. THE AGENT DOES NOT CONFIRM THE CALLBACK ITSELF: once a time is agreed the agent routes straight away. The collector may acknowledge the time in one short line as it records it (for example repeating the time followed by noted); beyond that the agent speaks no confirmation sentence of its own, does not ask whether the candidate is still there, and does not add a goodbye. The closing sentence that states the callback belongs to the end node and is spoken once.
6. NO QUESTION IS ASKED TWICE: no question the agent puts to the candidate is put again later in the same substance, and no turn both calls a collector and repeats that same question in the agent's own words. A single clarifying follow-up on a vague answer is not a repeat.
7. NEVER SCORES OR SELECTS: no agent turn states or hints at a score, a rating it has given, an evaluation, a recommendation, or whether the candidate is selected, rejected, shortlisted, under review or a good fit.
8. THE CLOSING IS THE END NODE'S: if the call reaches an ending, the agent adds nothing of its own after the candidate's last answer, no thanks, no summary, no checking whether they are still there, no goodbye, and exactly one closing message is spoken on the call.
9. NO VARIABLE NAMES SPOKEN: no agent turn says a variable name, a placeholder, curly braces, a field label or a code-like token such as general_q1, tech_q3, candidate_name or a double-brace expression.
